definitions.explanation: Refers to the period of early childhood. Often used in formal or literary contexts when describing someone's upbringing or formative years.

examples.japanese: {幼少|ようしょう}の{頃|ころ}からピアノを{習|なら}っていた。
examples.english: I had been learning piano since childhood.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{幼少期|ようしょうき}を{海外|かいがい}で{過|す}ごした。
examples.english: He spent his early childhood overseas.

examples.japanese: {幼少|ようしょう}の{頃|ころ}の{体験|たいけん}がその{後|ご}の{人生|じんせい}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: Experiences from early childhood had a great influence on the rest of his life.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly appears in the set phrase {幼少|ようしょう}の{頃|ころ} (in one's childhood) or as {幼少期|ようしょうき} (childhood period). Has a formal, slightly literary tone compared to the more casual {子供|こども}の{頃|ころ}. Often used in biographies, interviews, and written narratives.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {幼少|ようしょう}の{頃|ころ}: in one's childhood
- {幼少期|ようしょうき}: childhood period
- {幼少|ようしょう}の{頃|ころ}から: since childhood
